response: Yes, radiotherapy of the primary rectal cancer can affect prognosis after pelvic exenteration for recurrent rectal cancer. According to the available data, patients who previously received radiotherapy for primary rectal cancer treatment have worse oncologic outcomes than those who had not received radiotherapy after pelvic exenteration for locally recurrent rectal cancer. This suggests that radiotherapy for primary rectal cancer may have a negative impact on the prognosis of patients who undergo pelvic exenteration for recurrent rectal cancer.
